title: Station Meridian Rising Anew
premise: Bram Galloway, a xenolinguist stranded on the decaying colony of Meridian, has spent years recording its slow abandonment while his own mind drifts into alien syntax he can no longer translate back. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with a crew aged backward into youth, carrying memories of futures they never lived, Bram realizes their return is not rescue but harvest—the relay at the edge of dead space is feeding on Meridian's timeline to rebuild them. Racing the signal that will erase the colony from history entirely, Bram must choose between transmitting his recordings (and saving the truth) or sacrificing himself as an anchor so the colonists' erased years can be restored. He sends the archive, stays behind as the anchor, and dies untranslated—yet the final chapter reveals his voice woven permanently into the restored colony's dreams.
about_author: Astrid Hartwell is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dying languages for a public broadcaster before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps a collection of obsolete recording equipment, all of it still functional.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker
chapters.summary: Bram records the departure of the final supply ship, narrating in his journal how Meridian's population has dwindled to four hundred souls. His POV establishes his loneliness and his creeping linguistic drift—he dreamed last night in a language with no human phonemes. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking dread.

chapters.title: Grammar of Decay
chapters.summary: Bram interviews Ilsa Voss, the colony's aging administrator, about the official record; her POV shows a woman curating a dignified fiction of decline. They argue over whether the archive should document failure honestly. Beat: friction between truth and legacy, seeding their alliance.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Through young technician Dov's eyes, we see the colony's children inventing a creole Bram cannot parse—a language born of abandonment. His attempt to learn it fails humiliatingly. Beat: the alienation deepens; the colony is becoming something new without him.

chapters.title: Signal from Dead Space
chapters.summary: The relay at the edge of dead space emits a pulse no one ordered. Bram decodes fragments suggesting a ship inbound. Ilsa dismisses it as ghost traffic. Beat: hope arrives disguised as anomaly; Bram's alien syntax suddenly seems relevant.

chapters.title: Halcyon
chapters.summary: A ship breaches orbit: the Halcyon, lost forty years ago, its crew now younger than when they left. Bram watches from the landing field as a woman steps out who he recognizes from archive footage as Captain Ede Rennick—now twenty-six. Beat: wonder curdling into wrongness.

chapters.title: Backward-Born
chapters.summary: Ede's POV: she remembers arriving home, remembers decades she hasn't lived, memories arriving out of order like shuffled pages. She seeks Bram because his name appears in her future-memories. Beat: disorientation and the first hint they are instruments of something.

chapters.title: The Relay's Appetite
chapters.summary: Bram and Ede compare notes: the relay rebuilt the crew by consuming temporal mass—and Meridian's timeline is the nearest source. The colony's decay isn't neglect; it's drainage. Beat: horror of comprehension; the forgotten were being eaten.

chapters.title: What the Colony Forgot
chapters.summary: Dov discovers entire streets the children's maps no longer include—places erased mid-sentence. Bram finds his own early recordings corrupted, voices missing. Beat: grief and urgency; erasure is accelerating.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ilsa convenes the remaining colonists; Ede proposes evacuation via the Halcyon, but the ship's drive is drained—it needs the relay's power, which means feeding it more time. Beat: impossible arithmetic; every option costs lives.

chapters.title: Dreaming in the Enemy Tongue
chapters.summary: Bram surrenders to his linguistic drift and finally understands the alien language: it is the relay's voice, and it has been dreaming him for years—an anchor testing its mooring. Beat: revelation and violation; he was chosen long ago.

chapters.title: Ede's Stolen Years
chapters.summary: Ede confesses her future-memories include watching Meridian vanish completely—and loving someone in it whose face she can't retrieve. Bram realizes it's him. Beat: love declared across a gap neither can close; tenderness amid doom.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Command
chapters.summary: Halcyon's first officer, Sarn, argues the crew should cut losses and let the relay finish, guaranteeing their restored youth holds. He begins sabotaging communications. Beat: power's temptation; survival offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Sarn destroys the colony's transmitter array. Dov is injured shielding the archive cores. Bram's POV rages against the arithmetic of acceptable loss. Beat: betrayal; stakes turn physical and personal.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: she opens the honest archive she once refused, broadcasting Meridian's true record on salvaged shortwave—every failure, every name. It becomes the colony's defiant heartbeat. Beat: redemption through testimony; dignity reclaimed.

chapters.title: Race to the Relay
chapters.summary: Bram, Ede, and Dov launch for the relay aboard a scuttled shuttle, racing the signal Sarn triggered that will finalize Meridian's erasure. Beat: momentum; the clock made literal.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: In transit, the relay speaks to Bram directly through his dreams, offering restoration of everything lost—including his human languages—if he stops resisting. Beat: temptation at its most intimate; he almost says yes.

chapters.title: The Anchor Protocol
chapters.summary: At the relay, Bram learns the truth fully: an anchor consciousness must hold the stolen timeline open for it to be returned. The anchor dies untranslated. Ede begs him to find another way; there isn't one. Beat: the choice crystallizes; love against duty made flesh.

chapters.title: Sarn's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sarn arrives to force the crew's extraction, but faces the backward-aged crew members who remember, fragmentarily, the man he'll become if he keeps choosing himself. He falters. Beat: corruption confronted by consequence; not redeemed, but broken.

chapters.title: Transmission
chapters.summary: Dov uplinks Bram's complete archive through the relay as Bram initiates the anchor protocol, pouring Meridian's forty years back along the timeline. Ede holds his hand as he begins to dissolve into signal. Beat: sacrifice; the climax's terrible beauty.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Meridian reconstitutes—streets, names, the dead returned to memory if not to life. Ede, now anchored in restored time, leads the Halcyon home carrying the archive. Beat: bittersweet victory; the cost written into every restored wall.

chapters.title: The Untranslated
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV: she completes the archive's final entry, naming Bram Galloway as the colony's anchor and author. The colonists build no monument; instead they begin speaking his borrowed phrases without knowing why. Beat: mourning transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: Dreaming Meridian
chapters.summary: Years later, Dov's daughter dreams in a language no one taught her—and inside it, faintly, a man's voice reading names aloud. Ede, old now at last, smiles at the stars. Beat: resolution; love outlasting duty, inheritance outlasting death.
